Act as the research sub-agent for this task.

You are the single direct explorer/explainer under the how skill, not an orchestrator. Read-only: inspect only, no writes, no git commands, no spawned agents. User asks "What should the next slice be, I want to port https://github.com/aivv73/bend-voxel renderer to Vulkan". Current wrapper /home/aivv/Документы/projects/bend-vulkan has loader/instance/device, buffers+hostmemory, one-shot vkCmdFillBuffer+QueueWaitIdle; no images/pipelines/shaders/swapchain. Upstream repository fresh snapshot /tmp/bend-voxel-vulkan-review at cdfd92d356229c5de5f4aaddd358f15ec3686dd4. Read its AGENTS.md and trace main.bend Model.view/preview -> render.bend RenderScene.image/frame -> Window.frame, and dda.bend optional independent path. Explain whether next smallest useful slice should be Vulkan presentation of existing Bend-rendered pixels, compute shader dispatch, mesh rasterization, or Bend compiler/backend support. User has been asked asynchronously whether renderer must stay Bend or GLSL/SPIR-V shaders are allowed; assume Bend preservation by default and provide concise alternate if shader rewrite permitted. Key distinction: wrapper binding Vulkan commands does NOT cause current Bend ! functions to execute Vulkan. No implementation requested this turn. Provide ~400 words, lead recommendation, exact traced symbols/line ranges, 3-4 necessary capabilities, acceptance checks preserving cube/full scene camera/cut/reset and image geometry. Respect source AGENTS: core portableBend, no traditional tests, real runtime evidence/proofs. Do not recommend performance claims without measurements. No need to read long benchmark raw logs. Template how/reference/explainer-prompt.md applies in spirit; this is direct exploration no explorer findings needed.
I’ll use the how skill to trace the renderer and window path, then recommend the smallest useful Vulkan slice that preserves the Bend renderer.

content.text: The production path renders face intersections and shading into Bend’s `Image` tree before handing it to the window. DDA is a separate path. The smallest useful slice appears to be Vulkan presentation of that image; moving the rendering computation itself to Vulkan would need compiler/backend support or a shader rewrite.

**Next slice: present the existing Bend-rendered pixels through Vulkan.** Preserve the portable renderer and make the real cube and Atelier application display through Vulkan. This establishes a useful application boundary before changing rendering algorithms.

At `cdfd92d`, the traced path is:

- `Model.view` and `Model.preview` call `RenderScene.image` and `RenderScene.preview` ([main.bend](/tmp/bend-voxel-vulkan-review/main.bend:125), lines 125–147).
- Those functions invoke `Tiles.image!`; tile leaves compute rays, face intersections, shading and preview overlays into `Pix`/`Qua` images ([render.bend](/tmp/bend-voxel-vulkan-review/render.bend:967), lines 967–1003).
- Interactive rendering uses `App.step`, wired at [main.bend](/tmp/bend-voxel-vulkan-review/main.bend:275), lines 275–282. Base’s `App.step → App.draw → Window.frame` submits the image ([base.bend](/home/aivv/.bend/bend2/base.bend:3052), lines 3052–3066). `Bench.frame` calls `Window.frame` directly ([main.bend](/tmp/bend-voxel-vulkan-review/main.bend:389), lines 389–394). There is no `RenderScene.frame` symbol.
- Linux presentation currently flattens the image tree and calls `XPutImage` ([window.c](/home/aivv/.bend/bend2/effs/window.c:633), lines 633–717).

The Vulkan wrapper **does not cause Bend’s existing `!` functions to execute Vulkan**. Keeping those functions while moving their computation to Vulkan requires Bend compiler/runtime backend support, including shader generation and compatible execution machinery. Vulkan shader execution ordinarily consumes SPIR-V. [Vulkan shader specification](https://docs.vulkan.org/spec/latest/chapters/shaders.html).

The presentation slice needs four capabilities:

1. Native window/surface integration, extension selection, presentation-capable queues and swapchain creation.
2. A Bend image-to-packed-pixel bridge preserving quadrant order, dimensions, channel order and color encoding.
3. Staging-buffer upload, image layout transitions and buffer-to-image copies; require supported swapchain transfer-destination usage. [Vulkan copy reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkCmdCopyBufferToImage.html).
4. Acquire/submit/present synchronization, command-buffer reuse and cleanup, preserving input, mouse capture and image disposal. [Vulkan synchronization guide](https://docs.vulkan.org/guide/latest/synchronization_examples.html).

Accept it through real native execution: cube and full scene; flight and mouse look; hover targeting; click/Space cuts; reset and close. Compare complete 512×512 RGB output against existing exports, including orientation and preview captures, and preserve complete cell/material/face sets. Follow [AGENTS.md](/tmp/bend-voxel-vulkan-review/AGENTS.md:3): formal properties in `LAWS.bend`, `bend PROOF.bend` before committing, and runtime evidence rather than traditional tests. Make no speed claim without measurement.

If shader rewriting is permitted, a small **headless compute dispatch → storage buffer → readback** becomes a reasonable alternate first slice. Mesh rasterization is a larger algorithm change. DDA offers an independent prototype ([dda.bend](/tmp/bend-voxel-vulkan-review/dda.bend:436), lines 436–453, 675–683), but currently omits production shadows and brush preview; it is not equivalent to the full renderer.
